structured_output.summary: Attempt 4 is a mechanically proven additive overlay on corrected source. Both attempt-3 lows are fixed with new regressions: typescript035_profiles.py:113-116 now raises an explicit named error for unmatched upstream protection keys (test at test_typescript035_profiles.py:12-19), and the Request-only Zod-equivalence bound is recorded in contracts/typescript-035-parity.json:177 (test at :21-31). I independently confirmed the pinned upstream shapes, exactly five projected field occurrences in generated.rs, lossless typed-wins projection, the two new public types, the bounded list-default alias with an intact 23-binding denominator, 906 oracle cases / 231 accepted, and that all 107 recorded checks exit 0 on the reviewed SHA across both compilers and the full feature matrix. Two residual lows only.

findings.description: Zod-to-Rust replay still runs only in Mode::Request. For the six versioned clones that is deliberate, but ContentTypeConfigurationSchema and ContentTypeConfigurationsSchema are brand-new roots with no frozen legacy, so Mode::Response / Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults acceptance for them is asserted by no oracle. The attempt-3 finding was closed by documenting the bound (contracts/typescript-035-parity.json:177) rather than closing it; since these roots have no tolerant legacy and no defaults, replaying them in both response modes is a two-line change that would remove the last unexercised acceptance surface on newly minted public schemas.
findings.required_fix: Extend the replay loop to also run Mode::Response and Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults for case schemas starting with "ContentType", asserting identical acceptance and output.

findings.description: The historical-digest regression substitutes a bare hardcoded literal ('c81f053f…') for provenance.generatorSha256 before comparing to the pinned ddc0f2ac… digest. The literal is the pre-change oracle hash, but nothing in this file ties it to the Git baseline bytes; the baseline comparison lives in a different file (tools/test_typescript035_implementation.py:37-43). A future wrong literal here would silently weaken this pin while the test still passes.
findings.required_fix: Derive the substituted value from the Git baseline blob (as test_typescript035_implementation.py does) or add an inline assertion that the literal equals the baseline provenance.generatorSha256.

I read no credential or tenant-registration files, used no .local/typescript checkout and made no network calls. The historical frozen schema oracle check is recorded as invoked via .local/typescript/node_modules/.bin/tsx (checks artifact :2093-2105); I treated its recorded output as evidence without inspecting that checkout.

crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/schema_graph.json and semantics.json are single-line minified artifacts; I verified the new roots, the s_ts035 node set and the single s_ts035 semantic entry by targeted grep plus the generator reconstruction path (typescript035_profiles.py --check) and the Python/Rust regressions, not by reading them end to end. Likewise contracts/native-models.json and contracts/response-defaults.json were spot-checked at their supplemental sections rather than read whole.

Oracle-to-Rust equivalence is Mode::Request only (finding 1). I independently recounted 906 case ids and 231 accepted outcomes in the committed corpus but did not re-derive the Zod outcomes themselves.

Wire-chunk artifacts (profiles.rs, management_contracts.rs, the example, CHANGELOG/STABILITY/DIRECTIONAL_PROFILES, check_phase.py, Cargo.lock) were read only insofar as they evidence this chunk's model/validation claims; they are scored under wire-and-compatibility. I did not re-audit the frozen 0.34.0 baseline, historical phase 19-24 infrastructure or release receipts beyond the identity checks this overlay depends on.

Directional live/service acceptance remains explicitly unestablished and I did not assess it. One documentation gap I noticed but did not score here, because the files are wire-chunk scope: docs/STABILITY.md:36-48 and docs/DIRECTIONAL_PROFILES.md:103-118 describe typed-wins and tolerant responses but never state outright that consumers who previously read these four wire keys from `extensions` must now read the typed fields for representable values.
